label: Acts 10:1
text: Now there was a certain man in Caesarea, Cornelius by name, a centurion of what was called the Italian Regiment,

label: Acts 10:2
text: a devout man, and one who feared God with all his house, who gave gifts for the needy generously to the people, and always prayed to God.

label: Acts 10:3
text: At about the ninth hour of the day, he clearly saw in a vision an angel of God coming to him, and saying to him, “Cornelius!”

label: Acts 10:4
text:
He, fastening his eyes on him, and being frightened, said, “What is it, Lord?”
He said to him, “Your prayers and your gifts to the needy have gone up for a memorial before God.

label: Acts 10:5
text: Now send men to Joppa, and get Simon, who is also called Peter.

label: Acts 10:6
text: He lodges with a tanner named Simon, whose house is by the seaside.

label: Acts 10:7
text: When the angel who spoke to him had departed, Cornelius called two of his household servants and a devout soldier of those who waited on him continually.

label: Acts 10:8
text: Having explained everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.

label: Acts 10:9
text: Now on the next day as they were on their journey, and got close to the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray at about noon.

label: Acts 10:10
text: He became hungry and desired to eat, but while they were preparing, he fell into a trance.

label: Acts 10:11
text: He saw heaven opened and a certain container descending to him, like a great sheet let down by four corners on the earth,

label: Acts 10:12
text: in which were all kinds of four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, reptiles, and birds of the sky.

label: Acts 10:13
text:
A voice came to him,
“Rise, Peter, kill and eat!”

variants.note: Wikipedia, Papyrus 45, Some notable readings: 'Acts 10:13 Πέτρε (Peter): Omit.: 𝔓45 gig Clement Ambrose'. The WEB prints 'Rise, Peter, kill and eat!'.

label: Acts 10:14
text: But Peter said, “Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten anything that is common or unclean.”

label: Acts 10:15
text:
A voice came to him again the second time,
“What God has cleansed, you must not call unclean.”

label: Acts 10:16
text: This was done three times, and immediately the vessel was received up into heaven.

variants.note: Wikipedia, Papyrus 45, Some notable readings: 'Acts 10:16 εὐθὺς (immediately): Omit.: 𝔓45 36 453 1175 2818 it d syr p sa mss bo ms'.

label: Acts 10:17
text: Now while Peter was very perplexed in himself what the vision which he had seen might mean, behold, the men who were sent by Cornelius, having made inquiry for Simon’s house, stood before the gate,

label: Acts 10:18
text: and called and asked whether Simon, who was also called Peter, was lodging there.

label: Acts 10:19
text:
While Peter was pondering the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Behold, three
 men seek you.

label: Acts 10:20
text: But arise, get down, and go with them, doubting nothing; for I have sent them.”

label: Acts 10:21
text: Peter went down to the men, and said, “Behold, I am he whom you seek. Why have you come?”

label: Acts 10:22
text: They said, “Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man and one who fears God, and well spoken of by all the nation of the Jews, was directed by a holy angel to invite you to his house, and to listen to what you say.”

label: Acts 10:23
text: So he called them in and provided a place to stay. On the next day Peter arose and went out with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa accompanied him.

label: Acts 10:24
text: On the next day they entered into Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his relatives and his near friends.

label: Acts 10:25
text: When Peter entered, Cornelius met him, fell down at his feet, and worshiped him.

label: Acts 10:26
text: But Peter raised him up, saying, “Stand up! I myself am also a man.”

label: Acts 10:27
text: As he talked with him, he went in and found many gathered together.

label: Acts 10:28
text: He said to them, “You yourselves know how it is an unlawful thing for a man who is a Jew to join himself or come to one of another nation, but God has shown me that I shouldn’t call any man unholy or unclean.

label: Acts 10:29
text: Therefore also I came without complaint when I was sent for. I ask therefore, why did you send for me?”

label: Acts 10:30
text: Cornelius said, “Four days ago, I was fasting until this hour, and at the ninth hour, I prayed in my house, and behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing,

label: Acts 10:31
text: and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer is heard, and your gifts to the needy are remembered in the sight of God.

label: Acts 10:32
text: Send therefore to Joppa, and summon Simon, who is also called Peter. He lodges in the house of a tanner named Simon, by the seaside. When he comes, he will speak to you.’

label: Acts 10:33
text: Therefore I sent to you at once, and it was good of you to come. Now therefore we are all here present in the sight of God to hear all things that have been commanded you by God.”

variants.reading: κυρίου (Lord) where the WEB reads 'commanded you by God'
variants.note: Wikipedia, Papyrus 45, Some notable readings: 'Acts 10:33 κυρίου (Lord): 𝔓45 (vid) א A B C E Ψ 81* ...', against θεου (God): 𝔓74 D Byz syr p sa mae bo ms. The WEB keeps 'God'.

label: Acts 10:34
text: Peter opened his mouth and said, “Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism;

label: Acts 10:35
text: but in every nation he who fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.

label: Acts 10:36
text: The word which he sent to the children of Israel, preaching good news of peace by Jesus Christ—he is Lord of all—

label: Acts 10:37
text: you yourselves know what happened, which was proclaimed throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached;

label: Acts 10:38
text: even Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.

label: Acts 10:39
text: We are witnesses of everything he did both in the country of the Jews, and in Jerusalem; whom they also killed, hanging him on a tree.

label: Acts 10:40
text: God raised him up the third day, and gave him to be revealed,

label: Acts 10:41
text: not to all the people, but to witnesses who were chosen before by God, to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.

label: Acts 10:42
text: He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that this is he who is appointed by God as the Judge of the living and the dead.

label: Acts 10:43
text: All the prophets testify about him, that through his name everyone who believes in him will receive remission of sins.”

label: Acts 10:44
text: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all those who heard the word.

label: Acts 10:45
text: They of the circumcision who believed were amazed, as many as came with Peter, because the gift of the Holy Spirit was also poured out on the Gentiles.

label: Acts 10:46
text:
For they heard them speaking in other languages and magnifying God.
Then Peter answered,

label: Acts 10:47
text: “Can anyone forbid these people from being baptized with water? They have received the Holy Spirit just like us.”

label: Acts 10:48
text: He commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay some days.

label: A centurion named Cornelius, of the Italian cohort, lived in Caesarea
statement: There was in Caesarea a centurion named Cornelius, of what was called the Italian cohort (speira he kaloumene Italike). No independent source names Cornelius.
note: The CIL XVI 106 diploma attests the unit's name, not this man; the Caesarea setting is attested separately.

label: The Roman army in Judea included a cohort called the Italian
statement: The Roman forces in Judea in the 30s CE included a cohort (speira) called 'Italian' (Italike).
note: The unit is otherwise attested only in Syria (ca. 69-157 CE per the CIL XVI 106 diploma and the unit's Wikipedia infobox), not in Judea in the 30s.

label: Caesarea Maritima was the Roman administrative and military capital of Judea
statement: Caesarea Maritima, Herod's port city on the Mediterranean (with the Sebastos harbour), was the civilian and military capital of Roman Judea and the official residence of its governors, including the prefect Pontius Pilate.
note: The Italian-cohort centurion's station at Caesarea fits the garrison city Josephus describes (War 2.18.7).

label: Cornelius was a devout 'God-fearer' - a Gentile sympathizer to Judaism
statement: Cornelius feared God with all his house, gave alms generously and prayed constantly - the profile of a Gentile sympathizer ('God-fearer') to Judaism.
note: The Aphrodisias stele shows theosebeis as a technical category, but in 3rd-century Caria, not Cornelius himself.

label: Housetops were used for prayer at midday
statement: Peter went up on the housetop of the house in Joppa to pray at about noon - the flat roof as an inhabited, prayer-ready space.
note: Miracle-adjacent setting detail; recorded as a custom claim.

label: An angel appeared to Cornelius and told him to send for Peter
statement: At about the ninth hour Cornelius saw plainly in a vision an angel of God, who told him his prayers and alms were remembered and to send men to Joppa for Simon Peter (10:3-6, 30-32).
note: A miracle claim, recorded as such; no independent evidence.

label: Peter saw a vision of a sheet with all kinds of animals and a voice: 'kill and eat'
statement: In a trance Peter saw heaven opened and a great sheet let down by four corners holding all kinds of four-footed animals, wild beasts, reptiles and birds; a voice said 'Rise, Peter, kill and eat', and this happened three times.
note: A miracle/vision claim, recorded as such. Retold in Acts 11:5-10.

label: Judean Jews such as Peter kept the Levitical food laws
statement: Peter had never eaten anything common or unclean - observance of the Levitical distinction between clean and unclean animals (Leviticus 11).
note: Cross-referenced to Leviticus 11; no independent ancient evidence node was found for first-century Judean practice.

label: Cornelius was well spoken of by the whole Jewish nation
statement: Cornelius was reported to be a righteous, God-fearing man well spoken of by the whole nation of the Jews.
note: Character report within the narrative; no external evidence.

label: Jews avoided keeping company or eating with people of another nation
statement: It was unlawful (or contrary to custom) for a Jew to join himself to or come to one of another nation - the avoidance of Gentile company, especially table-fellowship.
note: Graded on the custom, not on the word 'unlawful' (the verb anomos is used loosely for a customary rule).

label: Cornelius prayed at the ninth hour
statement: Cornelius was fasting and prayed in his house at the ninth hour (mid-afternoon) - the same prayer hour as the temple's afternoon rite.
note: Differs from claim:ac-03-01-ninth-hour-prayer (Peter and John going up to the temple): a Gentile's private prayer at the temple's hour.

label: The Holy Spirit fell on the Gentile hearers, who spoke in tongues
statement: While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit fell on all the Gentile hearers; the circumcision believers heard them speaking in tongues and magnifying God (10:44-46; retold 11:15).
note: A miracle claim, recorded as such; no independent evidence.

label: Cornelius and his household were baptized in water in the name of Jesus Christ
statement: Peter commanded that Cornelius and those with him, having received the Holy Spirit, be baptized with water in the name of Jesus Christ (10:47-48).
note: An event claim within the narrative; no independent evidence.
